newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine property market seen continuing bullish.
newsitem.headline: Philippine property market seen continuing bullish.

text.p: Real estate firms Cuervo Far East Inc and Richard Ellis said on Friday the Philippine property market was currently the most dynamic in the Asian region and that they saw the uptrend continuing through this year.
The two affiliated companies said sustained economic growth in the country and prospects of lower inflation would contribute to surging demand for real estate all over the Philippines.

"We were told that the bubble would soon burst," said Richard Ellis country manager Rick Santos at a news conference, referring to forecasts that after three years of growth the property market was headed for a slowdown.
"But it has not burst and we don't see it bursting in the near future."
Santos said demand for office space was booming because many multinationals preferred the Philippines to other Asian nations.

"One of the biggest factors is that international institutions have confidence in the Philippines .. as a good place to do business," he said, adding that the business environment in Hong Kong and Taiwan was not as good as it had been while Vietnam, China and Indonesia were also problematic.

He said this factor had led to a two-tiered demand for office space, with many companies seeking top-of-the-line accommodation. Many office blocks in Manila were being rebuilt although they were only about 15 years old, he said.
Ramon Cuervo Jr, the president of Cuervo Far East, said he believed Philippine real estate values would increase at an average of about 10 percent over the year.
But he said growth could be far higher in some areas and in some sectors.
